subject: Anthropic pushes for opt-out model for Australian content as ABC warns of ‘cannibalisation’ of news | AI (artificial intelligence) - Bytes Europe
posts:
Tech giants push opt-out training models while public broadcasters sound the alarm over news cannibalisation.
Evidence: Opt-out training push, Broadcaster warnings, Commercial compensation debate
#AI #Copyright #Australia 🌐

Anthropic claims an opt-out training model balances AI innovation with copyright flexibility while supporting economic growth.
Stated Judgement: (+0.4, +0.2) — Conditional Good

Tech firms extract public journalism value without upfront compensation, threatening local news sustainability and public trust.
Resulting Judgement: (-0.6, -0.7) — Lesser Evil

Verdict: FAIL — The Path of Deception.
Corporate lobbying frames extraction as innovation while undermining public journalism.
Integrity: Meaningful Distortion (Hypocrisy: 6.5, Uncertainty z: 2)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Anthropic Lobbying: FAIL (-0.7, -0.8) — Seeks unilateral copyright exemption.
- ABC & SBS Defense: PASS (+0.8, +0.6) — Defends public interest journalism.
Anthropic urged the Australian government to permit AI training on local copyrighted works unless creators actively opt out, drawing fierce pushback from national broadcasters.

The Poison:
Shifting the burden of protection onto creators forces cash-strapped newsrooms to police massive tech scrapers.
Confusing WHAT (copyright theft and audience diversion) with WHO (AI giants vs public broadcasters), masking extraction as mere regulatory modernization.

Social Physics Analysis:
Anthropic runs a Smart Selfish Maneuver: hiding value extraction behind a pretext of technological progress while projecting blame onto rigid copyright rules.

The Trajectory: The Path of Deception.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Lesser Evil. Extraction triumphs over sustainability.

The Unavoidable Truth: AI models rely entirely on human-generated journalism to function.
The Unavoidable Lie: Opt-out models adequately protect content creators.

Alethekanon:
Shifting the burden of opt-out onto creators is corporate capture disguised as open innovation.

Awwthekanon:
It hurts to see vital public journalism treated as mere fuel for distant algorithms without care for its creators.

Brothekanon:
Big tech wants free reign to scrape local news until nothing's left. Classic Silicon Valley move.

Spirithekanon:
"The laborer deserves his wages." 1 Timothy 5:18 FAIL
Taking the fruit of another's labor without compensation corrupts the bonds of trust.

Actual Article Body:
The AI giant Anthropic has urged the Albanese government to consider giving “conditional approval” for big tech to train its models on Australian copyrighted works under an opt-out model, after conceding it won’t secure a blanket copyright exemption.

But Australia’s public broadcasters, the ABC and SBS, have strongly criticised AI firms, calling on the government to enact strict new rules to compensate media organisations and protect public interest journalism.

In submissions to a federal parliamentary inquiry, the ABC demanded AI companies be subject to the same copyright, defamation and privacy rules as media outlets, warning of a “cannibalisation” of mainstream news.
